To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the ventral and dorsal SCN respond differently to light exposure late in the night and at dawn.
the NMDA receptor antagonists MK-801 and CPP block the induction of NGFI-A mRNA by light in the ventral, but not the dorsolateral, suprachiasmatica nucleus (SCN).

NMDA receptors play a role in the regulation of gene expression by both light and spontaneous circadian mechanisms, and that the effects of photic and spontaneous circadian regulation of gene expression may be mediated by separate mechanisms in different subdivisions of the SCN.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptors in mediating the photic and circadian regulation of immediate-early gene expression in the suprachiasmatical nucleus (SCN).
the role of N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptors in mediating photoregulation of gene expression in hamster supratchiasmatic nuclei (SCN) in the ventral and dorsal SCN.
the role of N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) glutamate receptors in the suprachiasmantic nucleus (SCN).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the NMDA receptors play an important role for the photic induction of the expression of immediate-early genes in the SCN.
the NMDA receptor is involved in photic input regulating gene expression in both SCN subdivisions at ZT 0 and in the ventral subdivision at ZT 18.
glutamatergics are important in mediating light-evoked expression in the SCN, but are also involved in the spontaneous expression of some of these genes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
NMDA receptor activation is involved in the photic regulation of IEGs in the SCN but not in circadian regulation of gene expression, with the exception of the junB gene in the dorsal SCN.

the effects of nocturnal light on gene expression in the SCN are mediated by a complex network of intercellular communication, involving different neurotransmitter systems, in different parts of the nucleus.

NMDA receptors play an important role mediating photic induction of gene expression in all SCN subdivisions, but that the effects in different subdivisions are mediated by different cellular mechanisms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effects of NMDA receptor antagonism on gene expression are different in different parts of the SCN and that the effects of light at dawn are different from those at night.
NMDA receptor blockade can be used to selectively inhibit light-induced gene expression in the ventral part of the SCN, but not in the dorsal SCN, at night.
there are differential mechanisms regulating photic regulation of IEGs and spontaneous expression in the SCN.
